source.check: returned unopposed: 'Colonel Howard has been selected to represent Castlecaulfield Rural Council division' (Northern Whig, 13 April 1933, p. 3, image read); no contest in any division at the nominations on 18 April (Belfast News-Letter, 19 April 1933, p. 14); he sits on the Finance and Joint Committees at the new council's statutory meeting on 6 June 1933 and was not among the three co-opted members (Mid-Ulster Mail, 10 June 1933, p. 5, image read)

note: Triennial election of the Dungannon rural district councillors, 1933. Nominations were received on 18 April 1933 and 'there will be no contests in any of the divisions' (Belfast News-Letter, 19 April 1933, p. 14). No poll was held; Tyrone's polling day was Wednesday 31 May 1933. Council-meeting method: the Unionist delegates selected Colonel R. J. Howard, J.P., for the Castlecaulfield division (Northern Whig, 13 April 1933, p. 3); there were no contests; he sat at the statutory meeting of 6 June 1933, where Mrs. Brown, Mr. M. Brown and Mr. William Moffatt were co-opted (Mid-Ulster Mail, 10 June 1933, p. 5). He was again returned for Castlecaulfield in 1936. Returned unopposed.
